hints.title: Bar Width and Limiting Height
hints.text: For each bar, what defines the widest horizontal rectangle that uses this bar's full vertical height?

hints.title: Boundary Determination by Smaller Bars
hints.text: A bar's rectangle extends left and right until encountering a bar shorter than itself. The width is determined by the first smaller bar on either side.

hints.title: Monotonic Increasing Index Tracking
hints.text: Traverse the histogram while maintaining indices of bars with increasing heights. When a shorter bar is encountered, resolve bars whose heights exceed the current height: calculate width using current index and preceding boundary, update maximum area, and push the adjusted starting position.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def largestRectangleArea(self, heights: list[int]) -> int:
        stack = []
        max_area = 0
        extended = heights + [0]
        for i, h in enumerate(extended):
            start = i
            while stack and stack[-1][1] > h:
                idx, prev_h = stack.pop()
                max_area = max(max_area, prev_h * (i - idx))
                start = idx
            stack.append((start, h))
        return max_area
```

variables: N: number of bars in histogram (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Every bar index is pushed and popped at most once, giving linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all pairs of left and right boundaries takes O(N^2) or O(N^3) time. For N = 10^5, N^2 = 10^10 operations which severely exceeds time limits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing indices in an auxiliary structure uses O(N) space to achieve linear O(N) time because every bar is pushed and popped at most once.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining monotonic increasing invariant, correct width calculation i - stack[-1] - 1 with sentinel/boundary handling, and single-pass execution.
